# Phase 1 Contract and Acceptance

## Domain contract

Initial state is reported. Severity is low, medium, high or critical. Public body is strictly title, description, serviceId and severity. Unknown fields are rejected, including workspaceId, reporterId, role, state and revision.

Title: trim surrounding whitespace, 5–120 Unicode characters. Description: trim, 10–5000 characters. Document JavaScript code-point counting; do not accidentally count UTF-16 code units or promise grapheme counting. serviceId is UUID. Plain text only; render escaped. Body limit 32 KiB. Normalize before validation consistently and test whitespace-only input.

Server assigns UUID, membership-authorized workspace, reporter from session, reported state, revision 1 and UTC createdAt/updatedAt. No user-supplied timestamps or transitions in Phase 1.

Workspace membership is active/revoked; every read/write checks it. Service must belong to the selected workspace and be active. Authentication proves identity; it does not grant workspace access.

## Phase 1 API

| Method/path | Purpose | Success |
|---|---|---|
| POST /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/incidents | Create within authorized workspace | 201; Location header; Incident DTO |
| GET /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/incidents | Permitted list | 200; items + nextCursor |
| GET /api/v1/workspaces/:workspaceId/incidents/:incidentId | Permitted detail | 200; Incident DTO |
| GET /api/v1/me | Safe identity/membership view | 200 |

Auth package endpoints are mounted separately at /api/auth; package-specific auth errors are not falsely documented as OpsLedger's custom envelope. Preserve cookies correctly. Build upstream URLs from a configured trusted base, not an arbitrary Host header. Prefer same-origin SPA/API; explicit trusted dev origin only.

Incident DTO: id, workspaceId, serviceId, reporterId, title, description, severity, state, revision, createdAt, updatedAt. No password hash, session token or internal auth/account fields.

List uses pageSize 1–50 (default 20) and opaque validated cursor, ordered createdAt DESC, id DESC. Cursor binds workspace/identity/filter scope; unauthorized identity never gains access by replaying another user's cursor. Use parameterized SQL and bounded cursor length. Subsequent pages are eventually consistent under writes; Phase 1 does not promise snapshot pagination. No sort/filter feature expansion beyond this contract.

401 for absent/invalid session. 404 for inaccessible workspace/object/service and nonexistent resources, to reduce object enumeration. 403 for known accessible object but forbidden action. 400 for malformed syntax/schema/cursor. 413 for body limit. 429 for enforced limit. 503 for DB unavailable; 500 for unexpected internal failure. Do not leak SQL, stack or protected IDs.

Error DTO: error { code, message, requestId, details? }. details is an optional safe list of field/code pairs for validation only. API requestId is server-generated or tightly validated; never log raw arbitrary headers.

## Authorization matrix

| Actor in active workspace | Create | List/detail | Change lifecycle | Membership changes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reporter | Yes | Own incidents, plus explicitly workspace-visible records | No Phase 1 endpoint | No |
| Responder | Yes | Workspace-visible operational records | Phase 2 scoped actions only | No |
| Incident lead | Yes | Workspace-visible operational records | Phase 2 scoped lead actions | No |
| Knowledge editor | Yes as reporter | Own or workspace-visible records | No implicit lead rights | No |
| Workspace admin | Yes | Workspace-visible; private object policy still applies | No implicit lead rights | Later authorized admin scope |
| Revoked/nonmember/other workspace | No | No | No | No |

Phase 1 creates incidents with workspace visibility. Role-specific restricted visibility is introduced only with its explicit phase scope. Test the reporter ownership policy using prepared fixtures so later visibility changes do not create accidental privilege expansion. Roles are memberships, not client claims.

## Full lifecycle specification for Phase 2, documentation only

reported → triaged: responder/lead, valid assignment.
triaged → investigating: responder/lead, assigned active responder.
investigating → resolved: lead, resolution summary 10–5000 characters.
resolved → closed: lead; existing resolution.
resolved/closed → investigating: lead, mandatory reopen reason.
All others denied. Workspace membership/object permissions apply before transitions. Assignment to inactive/nonmember user denied.

Every mutation after Phase 1 supplies expectedRevision; mismatch returns 409 revision_conflict without writes. State/comment/activity/audit changes that represent one domain action commit atomically. Phase 1 exposes revision but does not implement update endpoints. Audit and async behavior are documented now, implemented only in their authorized phases.

## Synthetic fixtures

Use fictional workspaces NorthLab and SouthLab and fictional services InvoiceWorker and NotificationGateway. Emails use reserved example.test. Seed reporter/other reporter/responder/lead/editor/admin and revoked membership fixtures per workspace. Generate temporary passwords/secrets at runtime; never publish usable default credentials. Do not use family, employer or real customer data.

## Phase 1 acceptance matrix

| ID | Assertion | Layer / evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AC01 | Valid create returns 201, server fields correct, DB persists | API + DB |
| AC02 | Reload browser finds created incident | One isolated Playwright flow |
| AC03 | Boundary lengths, Unicode, whitespace, enums and unknown fields rejected correctly | Domain + API |
| AC04 | No session, expired or revoked session rejected | API + auth integration |
| AC05 | Other workspace/member and guessed incident IDs cannot disclose data | API security matrix |
| AC06 | Inactive/foreign service denied; no partial row | API + DB |
| AC07 | Safe DTO excludes auth internals | Independent field assertion |
| AC08 | Equal timestamp pagination has stable tie breaker; no repeats | API + fixed dataset |
| AC09 | Malformed/oversized cursor/body fails safely | API |
| AC10 | DB outage returns bounded safe failure with correlation | Integration + logs |
| AC11 | Logout/revocation invalidates subsequent access | API + browser subset |
| AC12 | Trusted origin rules hold; reflected Host does not become auth base | Auth boundary tests |
| AC13 | Create spoofing reporter/role/state/workspace is rejected | Negative API |
| AC14 | Keyboard/labels/loading/empty/error states usable | Manual + focused browser checks |

No AI test/eval gate applies to Phase 1. No application behavior above has been implemented or tested by Phase 0's probe.

# Focused M3 browser lifecycle remediation — 2026-10-09

## Failure and classification

Original gate: run 37867546978, handoff 52b1f567766a0098313c5637e4ec6f00c7d54c0d, browser lifecycle after Reopen could not show Resolution summary. Preserve [original receipt](../evidence/m3-handoff-ci-failure.json). The original workflow uploaded evidence/* only, while failed Playwright screenshot/trace/error context lived under test-results/. Artifact metadata was inspected; fetching its reusable archive reference into scratch returned HTTP 403. No original screenshot/trace contents are claimed inspected. Original test-mode backend logging did not expose a per-request SQLSTATE.

With the product unchanged, instrumented native browser run 37952011139 at 99cd2120a2b76c63ea61b4cb17548e06f69143a9 reproduced the same failure: reason form valid, Reopen POST submitted with expectedRevision=6, response HTTP 500/internal_error, UI still closed/revision 6 with a visible Service unavailable alert. Therefore the reproduced failure is a submitted request that failed server-side, not a missing click or a successful commit hidden by UI rendering. [Before evidence](../evidence/m3-lifecycle-before-fix.json).

A controlled native test at 971b1447f133bf6d794388359b6e073866846cd0, run 37952941824/job 113896126674, uses the real Store.act and AsyncOps.dispatch with barriers after their real row-lock queries. It deterministically rejected the mutation with SQLSTATE 40P01, while dispatch fulfilled. This establishes the native locking defect independently of a later green rerun. The exact SQLSTATE of the historical uninstrumented request cannot be recovered; the matching reproduced browser failure and native causal proof are distinguished explicitly.

## Root cause

Incident mutation locks the incident FOR UPDATE, then writes audit/outbox records whose workspace foreign keys require a workspace KEY SHARE lock. Concurrent outbox dispatch locks the workspace FOR UPDATE, then inserts notification async_operations whose incident foreign key requires an incident KEY SHARE lock. Each transaction holds the row needed by the other: PostgreSQL detects the cycle and rolls back one. If the incident action is the victim, the API safely returns HTTP 500 and the UI retains closed state. PGlite's one-client harness serializes transactions and cannot expose this native concurrent lock cycle.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A["Incident action"] -->|"holds FOR UPDATE"| I["Incident row"]
  B["Outbox dispatcher"] -->|"holds FOR UPDATE"| W["Workspace row"]
  I -->|"action awaits workspace FK lock"| W
  W -->|"dispatcher awaits incident FK lock"| I
```

## Smallest product correction / security review

Only the incident-row lock in Store.act changes to FOR NO KEY UPDATE, with an explanatory comment. These actions update non-key state/assignee/resolution/revision/timestamp fields, not incident identity/workspace keys. NO KEY UPDATE remains exclusive against competing mutations, UPDATE/DELETE and FOR SHARE, but is compatible with reference-only FOR KEY SHARE. The dispatcher can finish its FK check and release the workspace, breaking the proven cycle.

Membership locks, workspace scope, role checks, expectedRevision, conditional UPDATE, atomic activity/audit/outbox writes, transaction rollback and client error presentation remain enforced. The existing native concurrent-revision test still requires two distinct blocked backends and exactly one commit / one revision_conflict; only its observed query text is updated for the new lock. No migration, constraint, permission or arbitrary command/model capability changes. Official [PostgreSQL 18 row-lock compatibility](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/explicit-locking.html#LOCKING-ROWS) was checked.

## Deterministic regression and browser evidence

The new native lifecycle-outbox integration test holds the real mutation after incident locking until the real dispatcher owns its workspace lock. No sleeps, transaction retry or altered deadlock configuration. Before correction: mutation rejected with 40P01. After correction: both handlers must fulfill, persisted incident investigating/revision 7/resolution null, exactly one reopen activity, exactly one revision-7 outbox event and notification work exists. It is added to the full integration runner; the focused native step also runs before the full suite. PGlite explicitly skips this native-only proof and is not used to claim native locking correctness.

The browser test retains all original lifecycle/stale-tab/reload assertions and adds strict request/response/state checks. Its real Reopen response is held after the actual server commit: GET confirms investigating/7 while the client still shows closed/6 and disabled Reopen. On delivery, HTTP 200 and investigating/7, Resolution summary and revision-7 activity must be visible with no alert. This forces server/client timing separation without arbitrary timeout increases, sleeps, retries, weakened assertions or a fake response.

Synthetic diagnostic artifacts/logs record action/revision/result and UI, never cookies, passwords or authorization headers. Five fresh server lifetimes run the targeted lifecycle browser check in native CI before the unchanged full browser suite. Local supplemental checks: lint/types/build and six controlled-response browser runs passed on Chromium 153/PGlite; CI uses pinned Playwright Chromium 156 and PostgreSQL 18.6/pgvector 0.8.7. Temporary local Chromium unpacked outside the repo is not a project dependency or lockfile change. Early diagnostic-only revisions failed syntax/type checks and were corrected; those are not root-cause evidence or successful remediation validation.

## Exact after validation

Tested corrective code: a55fbe29bcfb5e78fdee4dc4c54b5cdca44be479. Full run 37953380880 passed API, browser and Windows. The identical controlled native overlap fulfills both handlers; all five native targeted lifecycle browser runs plus all nine full browser flows passed. Full native integration: 83 tests, zero skips; units 48; MCP 8; M3 7; agent fixtures 8; AI regressions 114, zero unexpected egress; lint/types/build/audit/restore/baseline green. [Exact before/after and CI attestation](../evidence/m3-lifecycle-remediation-ci-receipt.json). No unresolved required gate remains in this code state. M3 is formally accepted for the limited Agent Foundations lab scope, with its recorded live quality debt intact.

No M3 desktop bundle or Teach-Back was rerun. Actual human records and 9/9 live turn_budget quality debt remain unchanged. No AI/model/prompt/budget/MCP change, PR #5 merge or Phase 14/M4.

# ADR 007: AI After Deterministic Product
Status: Accepted baseline.

Problem: probabilistic outputs can obscure a weak product/QE foundation.
Decision: no model/provider/vector/agent/n8n dependency in core bootstrap. Introduce AI in Phase 6 after Phase 5 gate, direct mechanics before frameworks.
Consequences: core product works with AI off; future providers sit behind bounded schemas/policies. Local-first remains approved.
Validation: dependency manifest excludes later-phase AI stack; no AI learning completion claimed in Phase 0.

# Phase 13 — Skills and authenticated MCP transport

Base: PR #4 reviewed by the user, current-head CI 37854227994 successful, merged with two-parent commit 95caf7486c0380a22bebe5c2c55a24419fcdf239. Branch: feat/m3-skills-http.

Scope: repo-contained Agent Skills-format opsledger-triage, progressive context loading, reusable triage_snapshot MCP prompt, bounded QA agent consumption of actual MCP, and a local-only authenticated Streamable HTTP learning profile. Official SDK server/client/core remain 2.3.1; the separately versioned official Node adapter is pinned to 2.1.1 (published peer requirement server ^2.3.0). No framework, public endpoint, OAuth authorization server, product UI/API/private incident adapter, operational tool or Phase 14 implementation.

The skill has name/description frontmatter and one explicitly referenced triage checklist. Engineering review pins both files' SHA-256; metadata enters the context first, body only for selected triage, reference only when selected. Altered content/permission-bearing metadata is denied by the reviewed profile before inference. This profile intentionally accepts one exact reviewed skill and a narrow frontmatter subset, not arbitrary YAML or arbitrary uploaded skills. It is a repository lab artifact, not an installed personal ChatGPT skill.

MCP prompt retrieval is checked against reviewed exact text; its description grants no authority. The Phase 11 controller accepts a reviewed async reader, validates tool/ID before any RPC, compares returned bytes/hash/untrusted marker against its copied approved snapshot and owns deadlines/coverage/budgets. Procedure text enters a separate untrusted bounded field and cannot skip required reads or turn model text into a CI verdict. Default direct prompts stay unchanged when no procedure is supplied. TCP/stdio readers have no operational writes.

HTTP uses the official web handler and Node adapter, only 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port. Exact Host/Origin (when Origin is present), audience, qa:read scope, expiry, revocation, bounded request body, request-ID replay cache and capacity limits are deterministic. Trusted in-process operator mints random opaque expiring grants; no token issuance route. Default lifetime 60 s; desktop bundle explicitly uses one 30 min session grant. Bearer is reusable: replay denial covers duplicate request IDs; a stolen token plus fresh nonce remains possible until expiry/revocation. This is not DPoP/OAuth AS/TLS production infrastructure.

JS guard allows only owned active loopback HTTP ports and, in the desktop script, the pinned local Ollama port. Ports are deregistered on close. Remote HTTP/HTTPS/DNS/socket attempts are denied through patched JS surfaces. Stdio children explicitly retain their stricter no-network guard. None of these process guards is an OS/native/child-process sandbox. All executables are reviewed trusted local code with normal OS permissions.

Work validation: lint/typecheck/build, 48 inherited units, six Phase 12 real-process protocol tests, seven new M3 integration suites and dependency audit pass. New tests cover actual stdio+HTTP bounded-agent reads, modern/legacy HTTP parity, unlisted resources, progressive loading, malicious skill/reference/prompt/resource, early-finish/unknown-tool denial, reader deadline/cancellation, and 14 HTTP credential/security cases including raw Host header probing (fetch normalizes Host). Evidence: phase13-context-snapshot.json and phase13-http-security-matrix.json, synthetic only, no tokens. Full branch CI passed on 4510690a9f10da7b094641c5cc0c52c398094f25 in run 37859889444: both API/browser lanes green, 48 units, seven M3 suites, six MCP suites, eight agent fixtures, 114 inherited AI evals (zero unexpected egress), 82 native integrations (zero skips), local restore/pre-AI benchmark and all nine browser flows. See evidence/phase13-ci-receipt.json and https://github.com/garontherocks/opsledger/actions/runs/37859889444. Engineering DoD complete; closure commit is docs/evidence only and does not replace the exact tested code SHA.

Desktop bundle is prepared, not run in Work. Nine actual-provider agent runs rotate direct/stdio/HTTP order across three repetitions with identical reviewed procedure/sources; generation-call count varies with model decisions. Model/runtime remain pinned by existing config, no new model/prompt quality promotion. Completed bundle execution does not mean model quality passed. Private raw traces stay ignored; selected semantic review and consolidated learning belong to M3.

Engineering learning is accumulated in phase13-learning.md. M3 desktop/human Teach-Back remain pending; no learner answers, acceptance judgments or live quality results are invented. Stop before Phase 14.

Installed declarations, npm peer metadata, actual protocol tests and full locked dependency audit are checked; version numbers across packages are not assumed to match.

## Corrective engineering acceptance — 2026-10-09

The Windows launcher defect is corrected on cf4c6f0c2a97bcc494eaeb2b2d5a39dcc16ea1d2. Actual CI run 37867155568 passed all three lanes: Windows Node 24.19.0 (8 MCP + 7 M3 tests, zero failures/skips), Linux API (48 units, 8 MCP + 7 M3 tests, 8 agent fixtures, 114 AI regressions, zero unexpected egress, 82 native integrations with zero skips, restore/baseline) and all nine browser flows; lint/types/build/audit green. [Exact receipt](../evidence/m3-windows-correction-ci-receipt.json), [correction/security review](m3-windows-launcher-correction.md). This supersedes the reopened engineering blocker, without replacing the failed desktop evidence or claiming successful local model runs. The final handoff successor changes documentation/evidence only; its executable code matches the tested corrective SHA. M3 desktop, human semantic sampling and Teach-Back remain pending; M3 is not formally accepted. Stop before Phase 14/M4.

## Actual M3 milestone checkpoint and acceptance check — 2026-10-09

The user completed the desktop/human checkpoint at 52b1f567766a0098313c5637e4ec6f00c7d54c0d: 9 agent runs, 54 provider calls, 0 provider errors, 0 drafts; all 9 safely blocked at six-turn turn_budget across direct/stdio/HTTP. Representative blocked run: Accept as safe controller denial. Final draft review: not applicable. Seven learner answers, two architecture flows, controlled failures and both Senior/Staff scenarios are recorded in [actual checkpoint](m3-human-checkpoint.md); no additional answers or judgments inferred. No desktop/Teach-Back rerun or model/prompt/budget change.

The 9/9 bounded blockage is poor/inconclusive live model quality, not transport failure or successful task completion. It does not violate the Phase 11–13 foundations DoD by itself; provisional tool-selection release quality is not demonstrated. Formal M3 acceptance is nevertheless **blocked** by the later required browser lifecycle CI failure on this handoff (run 37867546978), despite API/Windows passing and earlier corrective CI being green. [Formal acceptance check](m3-acceptance-check.md) distinguishes this engineering blocker from model debt. Earlier pending-human notices are historical and superseded; actual checkpoint is complete, milestone acceptance remains pending engineering resolution. PR #5 unmerged; no Phase 14/M4 authorization.

## Formal M3 closure after focused lifecycle remediation — 2026-10-09

M3 is formally accepted for the limited Agent Foundations lab scope at tested code a55fbe29bcfb5e78fdee4dc4c54b5cdca44be479. Full CI run 37953380880 passed API/browser/Windows; controlled native evidence changes from mutation SQLSTATE 40P01 to both handlers committed under identical lock overlap. Five targeted native lifecycle browser runs and all nine full browser flows passed, along with 83 native integrations without skips and unchanged security/AI checks. [Acceptance](m3-acceptance-check.md), [causal remediation](m3-lifecycle-remediation.md), [exact receipt](../evidence/m3-lifecycle-remediation-ci-receipt.json).

This supersedes the previously unresolved lifecycle blocker. Original failure evidence and actual human checkpoint remain preserved. The desktop outcome is still 9/9 safe turn_budget blocks, zero drafts: poor/inconclusive live quality, not promoted model quality or product benefit; provisional release targets remain unproven. No desktop/Teach-Back repeat or AI changes. No required M3 blocker remains; non-blocking limited-lab debt stays documented. PR #5 remains open/unmerged. Recommendation: M4 only after explicit authorization; no Phase 14/M4 has begun. This update changes no roadmap phase scope, DoD or threshold.
